why: Image 1 reads as a real corner of a room: the shallow focus, the night window with street bokeh, the layered stone wall and the hammered copper bowl on a pale oak shelf all feel like a photographer working with the room's own light, even with the odd black tab under the bowl. Image 2 is murky and smeared, with a flat reddish cast, chips that look computer-generated and wood grain that looks plastic, so it reads as a dim render, not a place.
